Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Medium: the proxy statement is not supplied, so board names, committee membership, holders above the reporting threshold and related-person transactions are not established; closing it needs the definitive proxy statement that the annual report incorporates by reference. - Medium: the executed amended credit agreement, the two indentures, the receivables financing agreement, the Celero equity purchase agreement and the guarantor list are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, new debt, liens and asset transfers rests on note summaries; closing it needs those documents. - Medium: Celero earnings before interest, margin, customer concentration and churn, pro forma earnings and synergy phasing are not supplied, so the price of USD 664.6 million cannot be set against earnings; closing it needs Celero financial statements or an issuer pro forma earnings statement. - Low: a sources and uses statement for the Celero financing and the price of the 2021 First American Payment Systems purchase are not supplied, so only the change in debt balances shows how Celero was funded and the two purchases cannot be ranked by size; closing it needs the issuer statements. - Low: sponsor fund vintage, life, fees and equity contribution are not stated because no sponsor is named, and the absence cannot be separated from the missing proxy statement. - Low: processing volumes, take rates, merchant counts for the existing Merchant Services book and check volumes by product are not supplied, so organic growth and the speed of check erosion rest on revenue alone. - Low: whether owned real property is inside the collateral is not stated, because the annual report says owned properties carry no mortgages while the facilities are secured by substantially all assets; closing it needs the security documents. - Low: customer and supplier concentration below the 10% threshold and the share of revenue from financial institutions are not supplied, so channel dependence on banks is described but not measured.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage jumped, and the 4.92x probably overstates the settled level because only two months of Celero earnings are in it. Reported net leverage rose from 3.28x at 30 June 2026 to 4.92x at 30 September 2026, and adjusted net leverage from 2.92x to 4.20x, because debt principal rose USD 660.5 million in one quarter while trailing earnings hold only two months of Celero. Against the issuer's full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 470 million to USD 480 million, net debt of USD 1,929.2 million is 4.10x to 4.02x, so a fuller-year reading is about 4x before any debt reduction. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a cautious view is that the leverage spike may be transient: before Celero, reported net leverage had fallen from 4.02x at FY2024 to 3.28x and adjusted net leverage to 2.92x, management said it had reached its 3x target, the 2026 outlook for adjusted EBITDA was raised in August and again in November, and the outlook implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA 9.6% to 19.1% above the prior-year quarter, a quarter that will hold three full months of Celero. On the outlook, net leverage would be about 4.02x to 4.10x before debt reduction, and cost synergies of more than USD 15 million are expected. The view would improve if year-end results show net debt falling, Celero earnings support the price and the covenant ratios show headroom. It would worsen if Print declines faster than the 5.7% of FY2025, if free cash flow falls below the outlook of about USD 200 million, or if payments to shareholders rise while leverage is high. # Deluxe Corp: source readiness as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Issuer: Deluxe Corp (Deluxe Corporation, NYSE: DLX), issuer id dlx-27996. As of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot, requested modules CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2, this module assesses whether the nine supplied issuer documents can support credit work on the quarter ended 2026-09-30 against FY2025. No objective was stated, so the objective is the pathway use case, and the run settings are not issuer evidence.

The document date is the date the document states: the signature date for the annual and quarterly reports (their filing dates are not stated) and the release date for the three releases. No upstream handoff was supplied to this module, so none is listed.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The nine supplied filings and releases support a filed-basis credit assessment of Deluxe at 30 September 2026, but not covenant headroom, lien detail or market-implied views, because the financing agreements, ratings and prices are missing.

Debt of USD 2,025.5 million principal is printed by instrument and reconciles to the maturity table, and liquidity of USD 264.7 million follows from the printed cash and revolver availability. Celero was consolidated for only two months of the quarter against its full acquisition debt, and no pro forma earnings figure is supplied, so any trailing leverage built from these filings mixes periods.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 21; calculation C-1; calculation C-4; calculation C-11
### Key findings

- The documents cover every period the requested work needs: the audited year to 31 December 2025, three quarterly reports to 30 September 2026 and four releases, with the latest report signed on 5 November 2026 and nothing later before the 18 November 2026 cutoff.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C-13

- Debt and liquidity are printed at instrument and facility level and cross-check to the printed totals, so the debt stack, the maturity wall and facility availability can be taken from the filings without reconstruction. The largest maturity year is 2029 at USD 985.0 million, when both note issues fall due.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C-4; calculation C-5

- The covenant package is printed as tests and levels only. The issuer states compliance but prints no covenant ratio, and the earnings measure the tests use is defined in a credit agreement that is not in the set, so headroom cannot be established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C-12

- The Celero acquisition closed on 31 July 2026, so the quarter holds two months of its earnings against the whole of its financing. The price appears as three figures that differ by definition and reconcile to each other.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C-9; calculation C-11
- The amended credit agreement replaces the covenant terms printed in the FY2025 annual report, so the latest quarterly report governs current terms and the earlier terms are kept as history only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a limited verdict is that the largest gap sits in public documents: the financing agreements are exhibits to the issuer filings, and the latest quarterly report names the one that governs. Adding the amended credit agreement and the two indentures would lift the legal and covenant capabilities from conditional to ready, and a pro forma earnings statement for Celero, if the issuer files one, would remove the trailing-period mismatch. The verdict would worsen only if a supplied document contradicted a printed total, and none did in the cross-checks.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 121–122; calculation C-4; calculation C-5
### Limitations
- No document after 5 November 2026 is supplied, so events between that date and the cutoff are not covered.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 52
- The earnings releases and the outlook are management statements and are not audited, and their comparable adjusted measures exclude a business exit that the quarterly reports do not adjust for.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 39
- The FY2024 annual report states amounts in thousands while later reports state millions, so figures taken from it need a unit conversion and keep their own quantity family.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 74

## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt financing of the Celero acquisition lifted net debt to 4.92x trailing reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026 from 3.28x at 30 June 2026, so creditors now carry materially higher leverage on earnings that include only two months of Celero.

Total debt was USD 2,004.1 million against USD 1,352.2 million three months earlier, and cash interest cover of 3.45x carries the same two-month mismatch. Liquidity was USD 264.7 million, made up of USD 74.9 million of cash and USD 189.8 million of undrawn revolver.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 18, 21; calculation C-4; calculation C-5; calculation C-17; calculation C-25
### Key findings

- Reported net leverage fell from 4.02x at FY2024 to 3.28x at 30 June 2026 as net debt declined by USD 151.4 million to USD 1,317.3 million and trailing reported EBITDA rose from USD 365.2 million to USD 402.2 million. Net debt then rose by USD 611.9 million in the third quarter, in which the USD 642.9 million cash purchase of Celero was funded with a larger term loan and USD 200.5 million drawn on the revolver, so the open question is whether combined earnings restore leverage toward the earlier level.
Basis: calculation C-1; calculation C-4; calculation C-5; calculation C-18; calculation C-23; calculation C-27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 18, 21

- On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, net leverage was 3.05x at 31 March 2026 and 2.92x at 30 June 2026 before rising to 4.20x at 30 September 2026. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 52.6 million in FY2025, from share-based compensation, restructuring, impairment and legal items, so the adjusted ratios stand beside the reported ones and not in place of them.
Basis: calculation C-19; calculation C-26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 51

- Trailing reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.45x at 30 September 2026 against 3.40x at FY2025 and 3.10x at FY2024. The USD 113.8 million of trailing cash interest holds only two months of interest on the enlarged debt, as the trailing EBITDA holds only two months of Celero, so the ratio is not a pro forma measure.
Basis: calculation C-25; calculation C-26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 56

- Operating cash flow was USD 215.9 million over nine months of 2026, USD 47.4 million above the prior year, and free cash flow of USD 134.9 million equals 44% of reported EBITDA. The issuer attributes part of the gain to lower income tax payments from the 2025 federal tax law changes, so part of the improvement reflects tax payments rather than operations.
Basis: calculation C-20; calculation C-21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 38, 44

- A financing outflow of USD 256.9 million in the nine months is the unwinding of settlement processing obligations, which fell from USD 275.0 million at FY2025 to USD 18.1 million at 30 September 2026, and is not debt repayment. The obligations are held against restricted settlement assets of USD 16.6 million at 30 September 2026 and USD 273.6 million at FY2025, so the balance is a pass-through float rather than borrowing, but it makes closing cash and the net change in cash a poor guide to cash generation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 66

- Liquidity fell from USD 416.5 million at FY2025 to USD 264.7 million at 30 September 2026 as revolver drawings rose from USD 13.0 million to USD 200.5 million. Principal due is small until 2029: USD 15.0 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 60.0 million in 2027 and USD 160.0 million in 2028, which includes the securitization facility, before USD 985.0 million in 2029.
Basis: calculation C-14; calculation C-17; calculation C-7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 108

- Reported EBITDA is calculated for FY2024 and FY2025 because the annual reports print only adjusted EBITDA, and debt is taken at carrying value, USD 21.4 million below principal. The Celero price appears as USD 625.0 million of cash consideration, USD 664.6 million of consideration transferred and USD 642.9 million of cash paid net of cash acquired, and each figure is kept for its own role.
Basis: calculation C-8; calculation C-9; calculation C-6; calculation C-23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 12, 18

- Claims outside the debt figure are mainly leases and service commitments: finance lease liabilities rose from USD 25.8 million at FY2025 to USD 75.3 million after a new 16-year facility lease of USD 49.6 million, operating lease liabilities are USD 42.8 million non-current, and service contract commitments were about USD 210.0 million at FY2025. The retiree plan is an asset of USD 136.5 million, and no factoring, supply-chain finance or consent decree funding appears.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 23–24; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 57, 110
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that the 4.92x overstates the strain is the two-month Celero contribution: the issuer raised its 2026 outlook for revenue and adjusted EBITDA after the closing and expects cost savings from combining the businesses, and the trailing earnings carry neither a full year of Celero nor any saving. A full-year or pro forma earnings figure for Celero, which the filings do not print, would lower the ratio by an amount that cannot be worked from the sources. The view would improve if a year-end balance sheet showed net debt falling toward the earlier level.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C-5
### Limitations
- Each interim ratio rests on trailing figures built from quarterly releases and reports that print one decimal, so the components carry rounding of about USD 0.1 million.
Basis: calculation C-25
- No balance sheet after 30 September 2026 exists in the sources, so the December dividend is the only post-balance-sheet event found and its cash amount is not stated.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
- The issuer cites a leverage target of three times without defining it, so the target is not compared with the ratios here.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_dlx_exhibit991050620268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

## Gaps

- High: Celero earnings for a full trailing period, pro forma EBITDA and pro forma interest are not supplied, so leverage and cover at 30 September 2026 mix two months of Celero earnings with its full financing; closing it needs an issuer statement of Celero or pro forma earnings.

- Medium: the covenant ratios the issuer reports and the earnings measure defined in the amended credit agreement are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable here; closing it needs the executed credit agreement and the issuer compliance figures.

- Medium: the legal rank and collateral of the 8.0% senior unsecured notes, the 8.125% senior secured notes and the securitization facility are not stated in the filings, so the debt stack shows only the two first lien facilities and the notes are left out of secured and senior subtotals; closing it needs the indentures and the intercreditor terms.

- Medium: reported EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2025 is not printed in the annual reports and is calculated here from net income, non-controlling interest, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization; closing it needs the issuer to print the measure for fiscal years.
- Low: the cash amount of the December 2026 dividend is not stated, so the post-balance-sheet net debt figures are not supplied; closing it needs the declared total or the record-date share count.

- Low: lines the issuer prints as a dash (the gain on sale of businesses for FY2025, both third quarters and nine months 2025, non-controlling interest for both third quarters, and several cash flow lines) and lines that appear in only one type of statement (the asset impairment charge in the annual income statements, and the residual commission buy-out, acquisition and holdback lines in the cash flow statements) are stated as not supplied rather than zero; closing it needs the issuer to state nil explicitly.

- Low: the 2025-12-31 balance sheet is presented differently in the 2026 reports, where finance lease liabilities are a separate line, so the FY2025 column keeps the annual report presentation and finance lease liabilities for FY2024 and FY2025 are not separately supplied.
- Low: the FY2024 revolver availability is printed in thousands in the FY2024 annual report only, and is restated here to one decimal in millions.

- Low: the margin grid and any floor of the term loan, the revolver and the securitization facility are not stated in the filings, so the debt instrument register shows weighted-average rates only; closing it needs the executed credit agreement and receivables financing agreement.
- Low: the issuer cites a three times leverage target without stating its definition, so the target cannot be compared with the ratios here.
- Low: the split of capital expenditure between maintenance and growth is not supplied, so only total capital expenditure is carried; closing it needs the issuer to disclose the split.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Deluxe's credit risk comes from its own debt-funded shift from checks to payments, not from an owner, because no sponsor or controlling holder is named, and the Celero purchase lifted debt to USD 2,004.1 million before the new earnings are proven.

Print is still the cash engine, with 54.9% of segment adjusted EBITDA on 46.3% of revenue in the nine months to 30 September 2026, so the payments and data segments must replace shrinking print earnings while carrying the new debt. Celero added USD 33.5 million of revenue in two months, and its earnings are not in the documents, so the price paid cannot be tested against them. The quarterly dividend of USD 0.30 per share continues inside a USD 75.0 million annual cap on dividends and repurchases.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14, 18, 20, 25–27; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-3; calculation C-11
### Key findings

- The business is a shrinking print franchise that still earns most of the profit, beside three growing segments that earn lower margins. Print was 53.3% of FY2025 revenue and 60.8% of segment adjusted EBITDA at a 32.3% margin, against margins of 21.6% to 28.1% in the other three segments, so replacing print earnings takes more revenue per dollar of EBITDA and leaves cash flow dependent on how fast the growth segments scale.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 113–115; calculation C-1; calculation C-8; calculation C-11

- Print is eroding steadily rather than collapsing. Print revenue declined 4.5% in FY2024 and 5.7% in FY2025, and 4.7% in the nine months to 30 September 2026 once the Safeguard sale is removed, while Print adjusted EBITDA fell USD 18.7 million and the three other segments added USD 32.1 million. The loss of print cash flow is gradual enough to plan around but does not stop.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 27, 29; calculation C-12; calculation C-13; calculation C-15; calculation C-29

- Celero is large relative to the segment it joins, yet nothing in the documents shows its earnings. The pro forma statement implies about USD 148.6 million of Celero revenue in the nine months of 2025, 50.0% of the USD 297.2 million of existing Merchant Services revenue, and Merchant Services grew 3.7% in the third quarter without Celero against 37.9% as reported, so reported growth in the segment is mostly acquired.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 26–27; calculation C-16; calculation C-17; calculation C-18

- The purchase was debt-funded and carries a heavy intangible component. Goodwill is USD 385.6 million, 58.0% of the USD 664.6 million consideration transferred, debt principal rose USD 660.5 million in the third quarter to USD 2,025.5 million, and a purchase multiple cannot be calculated because Celero earnings are not supplied, so creditors cannot test the price against earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 18; calculation C-19; calculation C-20

- No sponsor or controlling holder is named, which removes sponsor extraction as a documented risk and also removes any identified source of equity support. The common stock is listed with thousands of holders of record, but the proxy statement that would show large holders and related-person transactions is not supplied, so the absence is a limit of the documents and not proof of dispersed ownership.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 117–118

- Distributions are modest and capped. Dividends paid were USD 55.2 million in FY2025, 31.5% of free cash flow, no shares have been repurchased since the first quarter of 2020, and the amended credit agreement caps dividends and repurchases at USD 75.0 million a year, up from a USD 60.0 million cap that applied above 2.75x leverage. The cap leaves USD 19.8 million of room above the FY2025 dividend before further payments allowed by leverage tests whose terms are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 58; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C-21; calculation C-22

- Management's leverage target gives way to strategy. The first-quarter release says the 3x leverage target was reached, the Celero purchase was announced on 18 June 2026, and the amended credit agreement allows total leverage of 4.75x through 30 June 2027, so the covenant and not the target is the working limit on how far leverage can rise.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_dlx_exhibit991050620268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Acquisition appetite is a pattern: large purchases are funded with debt and small ones with cash. First American Payment Systems in 2021, which the issuer called the largest acquisition in its history, was financed with USD 500.0 million of 8.0% senior unsecured notes, the 2025 CheckMatch purchase cost USD 24.6 million in cash and a residual commission buy-out cost USD 36.0 million, while disposals are small, such as USD 22.8 million of net proceeds for Safeguard.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 21

- Disclosure supports monitoring of the base business but not of the acquired business or of legal capacity. The audit opinions are unqualified, internal control was effective at year-end 2025, covenant compliance is stated each quarter and segment results use the chief executive's measure, but Celero is excluded from the 2026 internal control assessment, covenant ratios are not printed and the executed agreements are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 66, 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 25, 50

- Customer concentration is low but channel dependence is high. No customer exceeded 10% of consolidated revenue in the last three years, yet checks, 32.3% of FY2025 revenue, reach customers through financial institutions and banks are the largest customer segment of Data Solutions, so bank consolidation or in-house moves would hit Print and Data Solutions together.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 113, 115; calculation C-7

- Sponsor and governance risk is Medium. The level is driven by a debt-funded acquisition that raised leverage while dividends continued, because that reduces the cash left for debt and leaves interest and covenant sensitivity higher, which implies weaker protection for creditors until deleveraging resumes; it is held at Medium and not High because no extraction, priming or sponsor behaviour is documented, and it cannot be firmer because the executed agreements and the proxy statement are missing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 18, 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 117–118; calculation C-20; calculation C-21
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the view that the transition is being financed at creditors' risk is that the growth segments are already delivering: payments and data revenue rose 14.6% and their adjusted EBITDA rose 18.0% in the nine months, management raised the 2026 outlook for adjusted EBITDA to USD 470 million to USD 480 million after the closing, cost synergies of more than USD 15 million are expected, and free cash flow of USD 134.9 million was 3.14x the USD 43.0 million of dividends paid. The view would improve if year-end results show debt falling and Celero earnings supporting the price. It would worsen if Print declines faster than the 4.5% to 5.7% yearly pace seen so far, if payments to shareholders rise while leverage is high, or if the executed agreements show baskets that let value move outside the creditor group.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 25, 27, 29; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-12; calculation C-21

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Deluxe bought Celero Commerce on 31 July 2026 for cash consideration of about USD 625.0 million plus seller transaction expenses and other adjustments, a purchase the issuer announced on 18 June 2026. The consideration transferred was USD 664.6 million, of which USD 385.6 million is goodwill and USD 258.0 million is intangible assets, and the allocation is still preliminary. Celero contributed USD 33.5 million of revenue and a net loss of USD 1.9 million in the two months it was owned, and management expects cost synergies of more than USD 15 million without giving a phasing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C-19

The documents state that the purchase was financed through the amended credit agreement with additional term loan borrowing and a revolver draw, and no equity issue or asset sale is described as a source. Debt principal rose USD 660.5 million in the third quarter to USD 2,025.5 million: the term loan rose USD 408.0 million to USD 800.0 million, revolver borrowings rose USD 194.5 million to USD 200.5 million and the securitization facility rose USD 58.0 million to USD 100.0 million. The amended and restated agreement of 31 July 2026 provides a USD 800.0 million first lien term loan and a USD 400.0 million first lien revolver, both due on 31 July 2031, with quarterly term loan instalments of USD 15.0 million from 31 December 2026 and debt issuance costs of USD 12.6 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 18–19; calculation C-20

Maximum total leverage under the amended agreement is 4.75x through 30 June 2027, then 4.25x for the next two quarters and 4.00x from 31 March 2028, and the cap on dividends and repurchases is USD 75.0 million a year. In July 2026 the issuer also entered interest rate swaps with a notional of USD 600.0 million at a fixed rate of 4.13% that mature in July 2030, and USD 500.5 million of debt stayed variable after the swaps. No new notes were issued in the nine months to 30 September 2026; the 2029 senior unsecured notes and the 2029 senior secured notes are unchanged.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 19–21, 36

The executed credit agreement, the equity purchase agreement and the guarantor list are not supplied, so lien priority of the notes, baskets for further debt and distributions, and any guarantee from Celero are not established. The issuer's pro forma statement gives revenue and net income but no earnings before interest, so a purchase multiple is not calculable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 20

- Medium: the proxy statement is not supplied, so board names, committee membership, holders above the reporting threshold and related-person transactions are not established; closing it needs the definitive proxy statement that the annual report incorporates by reference.

# Deluxe Corp: fundamental credit view as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Issuer: Deluxe Corp (Deluxe Corporation, issuer id dlx-27996), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the fundamental credit view, strengths and weaknesses, materiality ranking and monitoring signals, built on the supplied issuer documents and the accepted Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance modules of the same run. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size is given.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Deluxe's credit profile is adequate but weaker since the Celero purchase: print cash flow still carries the debt, yet reported net leverage rose to 4.92x and creditors now rely on acquired earnings and synergies the documents do not show.

Free cash flow of USD 175.3 million in FY2025 and liquidity of USD 264.7 million cover the USD 235.0 million of principal due before 2029, and the bank debt runs to 2031, so the first real test is the 2029 notes. Reported net leverage is above the 4.75x covenant ceiling that applies to June 2027, yet compliance is stated, so headroom depends on an earnings definition that is not supplied and cannot be calculated. The net debt and leverage after the dividend payable on 1 December 2026 are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; calculation C-1; calculation C-12
### Key findings

- Leverage jumped, and the 4.92x probably overstates the settled level because only two months of Celero earnings are in it. Reported net leverage rose from 3.28x at 30 June 2026 to 4.92x at 30 September 2026, and adjusted net leverage from 2.92x to 4.20x, because debt principal rose USD 660.5 million in one quarter while trailing earnings hold only two months of Celero. Against the issuer's full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook of USD 470 million to USD 480 million, net debt of USD 1,929.2 million is 4.10x to 4.02x, so a fuller-year reading is about 4x before any debt reduction. The net debt after the dividend payable on 1 December 2026 is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-5; calculation C-6

- Cash generation is the main support, and it improved. Free cash flow rose 75.3% to USD 175.3 million in FY2025, 46.3% of reported EBITDA, and was USD 134.9 million in the first nine months of 2026, on capital spending of 4.5% of revenue and dividends of 31.5% of free cash flow. After dividends of USD 56.6 million, trailing free cash flow of USD 157.7 million is only 8.2% of net debt, so deleveraging has to come from earnings growth as much as from repayment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-8; calculation C-13; calculation C-15

- Covenant headroom is the weakest-evidenced point. Reported net leverage of 4.92x is above the 4.75x total leverage ceiling that applies through 30 June 2027, and filed cash interest cover of 3.45x, on different definitions, is 0.45x above the 3.00x covenant minimum, yet the issuer states compliance at 30 September 2026. The covenant earnings and debt definitions sit in an agreement that is not supplied, so whether the gap reflects add-backs, pro forma Celero earnings or other terms is not established, and headroom is not calculable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12

- Refinancing risk sits in 2029, not before. Principal due before 2029 is USD 235.0 million against liquidity of USD 264.7 million, bank debt runs to 2031, and 88.4% of principal falls due from 2029; both note issues, USD 925.0 million together, mature in 2029 and the secured notes mature on 1 February 2029 if any unsecured notes remain outstanding. No rating, price or spread is in the documents, so market access is not established and refinancing capacity rests on how far leverage falls by then.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21; 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-1; calculation C-2; calculation C-3

- Liquidity is adequate for the near term but thinner. It fell by USD 151.8 million from FY2025 to USD 264.7 million, 13.2% of total debt, as the revolver draw reached USD 200.5 million, 50.1% of its commitment, and the securitization facility stands at its stated USD 100.0 million maximum, so it adds no headroom. The revolver is the only visible shock absorber.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-4

- Revenue durability is weak in Print and acceptable elsewhere, and reported growth overstates it. Print revenue declined 4.5% in FY2024 and 5.7% in FY2025 and provides 54.9% of segment adjusted EBITDA; payments and data revenue grew 14.6% in the nine months, but Merchant Services grew 3.7% in the third quarter without Celero against 37.9% as reported, so revenue of USD 2,126.4 million over the last twelve months is level with USD 2,133.2 million in FY2025.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; calculation C-14

- Margin resilience is average, because cost action is doing more than mix. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 22.2% in the nine months to 30 September 2026 from 20.4% as corporate costs fell USD 14.9 million and selling, general and administrative expense eased to 40.1% of revenue from 40.8%, yet revenue is moving toward lower-margin services and gross margin slipped to 51.9% from 53.3%. Further gains depend on more savings and on Celero cost synergies of more than USD 15 million, which have no stated phasing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 26, 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C-11

- Financial policy is a judgement call at medium risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, the quarterly dividend of USD 0.30 per share is modest and no extraction is documented, but management said in May 2026 that it had reached its 3x leverage target and then re-levered through a debt-funded purchase, and the amended agreement allows total leverage of 4.75x. The covenant, not the target, is the working limit on leverage.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-03-31_dlx_exhibit991050620268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20

- The primary downside path is faster print erosion arriving while Celero is unproven. As an illustration and not a forecast, a further Print revenue decline equal to the FY2025 dollar decline of USD 68.3 million would remove about USD 22.0 million of EBITDA at the Print margin of 32.3% with no cost action, taking trailing reported EBITDA to USD 370.3 million, net leverage to 5.21x and cash interest cover to 3.25x, while free cash flow of USD 192.3 million would still cover dividends 3.40x. Liquidity would carry the near term, so the pressure would fall on the covenant tests and on refinancing the 2029 notes at higher leverage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 114; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-9; calculation C-10
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a cautious view is that the leverage spike may be transient: before Celero, reported net leverage had fallen from 4.02x at FY2024 to 3.28x and adjusted net leverage to 2.92x, management said it had reached its 3x target, the 2026 outlook for adjusted EBITDA was raised in August and again in November, and the outlook implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA 9.6% to 19.1% above the prior-year quarter, a quarter that will hold three full months of Celero. On the outlook, net leverage would be about 4.02x to 4.10x before debt reduction, and cost synergies of more than USD 15 million are expected. The view would improve if year-end results show net debt falling, Celero earnings support the price and the covenant ratios show headroom. It would worsen if Print declines faster than the 5.7% of FY2025, if free cash flow falls below the outlook of about USD 200 million, or if payments to shareholders rise while leverage is high.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-03-31_dlx_exhibit991050620268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_exhibit991080520268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dlx_tm2621737d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C-6; calculation C-7
### Limitations

- The covenant ceilings cannot be tested because the agreement's earnings and debt definitions are not supplied; if its definition adds back more than the filed measure, headroom is wider than the filed ratios suggest, and if not, the leverage test would be tight, which would move the assessment of financial policy and refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C-12

- The leverage and downside figures mix two months of Celero earnings with its full debt and rest on management's outlook and one labelled sensitivity, not on a forecast, so the 4.92x and the 5.21x illustration both overstate or understate the settled position by an amount the documents do not allow to be measured.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-09-30_dlx_exhibit991110420268-k-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C-6; calculation C-10

- The documents contain no rating, bond price or spread, so ability to refinance rests on maturity structure and cash generation alone; market evidence of weak access would lower the refinancing view, and strong access would raise it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21

- The ownership and governance reading is limited to the annual report and the quarterly reports, because the proxy statement and executed agreements are not supplied; a large holder or related-party leakage in them would change the financial policy judgement.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 41
### Strengths and weaknesses

A strength is cash generation on low capital needs. Free cash flow of USD 175.3 million in FY2025 came from a Print margin of 32.3% and capital spending of 4.5% of revenue, which funds dividends of 31.5% of free cash flow and leaves cash for debt service, so the debt is carried by operating cash flow and not by asset sales.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 114; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-13; calculation C-15

A strength is the back-ended maturity profile. Bank debt runs to 2031, principal due before 2029 is USD 235.0 million against liquidity of USD 264.7 million, and the amended agreement removed the 2029 maturity of the bank facilities, so there is no near-term refinancing event.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-1

A strength is improving margins from cost action and growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 22.2% against 20.4% and payments and data growth of 14.6% in the nine months support earnings that can lower leverage if they persist.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-11; calculation C-14

A strength is policy without an owner to extract value: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, there is no buyback since the first quarter of 2020, and the dividend is capped at USD 75.0 million a year with FY2025 payments of USD 55.2 million.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 58

A weakness is leverage after the Celero purchase. Reported net leverage of 4.92x and adjusted net leverage of 4.20x rest on two months of acquired earnings, interest will carry the full debt, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated, so creditors bear execution risk on integration and synergies.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C-5; calculation C-12

A weakness is the steady erosion of Print, which is 54.9% of segment adjusted EBITDA and declined 4.5% to 5.7% a year, while the replacement segments earn lower margins and Merchant Services grew only 3.7% in the third quarter without Celero.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C-14

A weakness is the concentrated 2029 wall. USD 985.0 million is due in 2029, 88.4% of principal falls due from 2029, the secured notes spring to 1 February 2029 if unsecured notes remain, and no market evidence is supplied on access.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 21; 10-K_2024-12-31_dlx.htm.jsonl, page 64; calculation C-2; calculation C-3

A weakness is thinner liquidity. Liquidity fell USD 151.8 million to USD 264.7 million, the revolver is 50.1% drawn and the securitization facility has no headroom, so the revolver is the only visible buffer against a shock.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dlx.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-4
